title: Make generic staging and uninstall manifest-complete
summary: packaging/uninstall.sh was rewritten from a 66-line hardcoded-path script to a manifest-driven, DESTDIR-aware, idempotent uninstaller. It reads packaging/install-manifest.toml via python3 tomllib (same as stage.sh), reverses every declared path (files → generated_state → rmdir for dirs), purges /var/lib/namtor + /run/namtor, removes the namtor user and namtor-auth group (if existing), and disables PAM services before deleting the PAM module via namtor-pam-edit disable-all → lifecycle.sh pre-remove → grep+warn fallback. Forward staging (stage.sh --package all) + reverse uninstall = zero Nam-tor-owned file paths remain, zero Nam-tor-specific dirs remain, shared dirs with stock files correctly survive rmdir, dry-run touches nothing, interrupted uninstall resumes idempotently. 28 manifest-declared files removed, 4 generated-state paths purged, 13 dirs rmdir'd.

safety_invariants.pam_disabled_before_module_delete: PASS — the PAM module existed when namtor-pam-edit disable-all ran (verified via test stub that records module existence at call time)
safety_invariants.shared_dirs_preserved: PASS — /usr/share/applications, /usr/share/metainfo, /usr/lib/systemd/system survive (non-empty due to stock files; rmdir --ignore-fail-on-non-empty)
safety_invariants.dry_run_safe: PASS — 39 files before = 39 files after dry-run; pam_namtor.so still present
safety_invariants.idempotent_resume: PASS — partial removal (half files deleted manually) + full uninstall = zero leftovers; re-run exits 0
safety_invariants.no_hardcoded_paths: PASS — no `rm -f /usr/lib/namtor/namtor-daemon` or similar hardcoded paths in uninstall.sh; all paths derived from manifest via tomllib

files_not_touched: packaging/stage.sh — only verified, no changes needed (--package support intact)
packaging/install-manifest.toml — not modified; uninstall.sh is a consumer
packaging/lifecycle.sh — not modified; used as PAM-disabling fallback
distro packaging (arch/ fedora/ debian/) — out of scope; distro-specific hooks use their own maintainer scripts
